info.title: Jobmate API
info.description: Backend for the Jobmate Flutter app. All responses use the envelope { success, data, message } or { success, data, pagination }.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/admin/dashboard — the counts the admin home screen shows.
GET /api/v1/admin/verifications — the review queue.
get.description:
Pending requests oldest first, which is the order they should be worked in: each
one is somebody waiting for an answer. Add `status=rejected` to revisit
decisions, or `type=identity` to work one kind of check at a time.
            
The applicant's phone number is included so a document that looks wrong can be
checked with the person before it is refused.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/admin/verifications/{id}/approve — accepts the document.
post.description:
An empty body approves. Approving updates the applicant's trust badge straight away,
and the badge only turns green once all four consumer checks are approved, so this
is one step towards verified rather than verified itself.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/admin/verifications/{id}/reject — refuses it, with a reason.
post.description:
`rejectionReason` is required and is shown to the applicant verbatim, so it has
            to say what to fix — "photo too dark", not "rejected". The request keeps the reason,
            and the applicant can submit again afterwards.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/admin/users — the users table.
get.description:
The activity column means jobs posted for a work giver and applications made for a
worker. Filter with `role`, `isActive` or `verification`; search
matches name, email and phone number.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/admin/users/{id}/status — suspends or reinstates an account.
post.description:
A suspension, not a deletion: the account keeps its jobs, bookings and messages, so
reinstating it puts the person back where they were. The body is required, because
an absent body would otherwise read as "suspend".

get.summary: GET /api/v1/admin/jobs — the jobs table.
get.description:
Filter by `status` or `category`; search matches the title and the hiring
company. `applicants` is a count, so the table does not have to load every
application to draw a row.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/admin/jobs/{id} — the job detail panel.
get.description:
The row plus the two things an admin opens a job to find out: how much of the
applicant pipeline converted into bookings, and how much was actually paid.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/admin/auth/login — email and password, admin role only.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/admin/disputes — the dispute queue, open cases first.
get.description:
Defaults to the cases that are still live, oldest first, because those are the ones
somebody is waiting on. Pass `status=resolved` or `status=rejected` to
look at closed work, and `search` to match the description or the notes.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/admin/disputes/{id}/review — marks a dispute as being looked at.
post.description:
A separate step from resolving so the queue shows what has been picked up, and so a
second admin does not start duplicating work that is already in progress.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/admin/disputes/{id}/resolve — closes a dispute.
post.description:
Send `status=resolved` when the complaint was justified and
`status=rejected` when it was not; both need `resolution` saying why,
which is what both parties are shown. Closing a dispute releases any money it was
holding back to the worker. If the outcome goes against the worker, refund the
payment separately afterwards.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/admin/support-reports — the support report queue.
get.description:
Newest first, showing handled reports too. Add `isResolved=false` for just the
outstanding ones.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/admin/support-reports/{id}/resolve — marks a report dealt with.
post.description:
Send `isResolved=false` to put it back, for a report that turned out to need
more work rather than one that was filed in error.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/applications/{id}/withdraw — the worker takes back their application.
post.description:
Only the worker who applied may do this, and only while the application is still
open: a rejected, withdrawn or expired one is terminal.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/applications/{id}/shortlist — the giver keeps this applicant.
post.description: Send `proposedPay` to attach an offer the app shows on the applicant card.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/applications/{id}/reject — the giver turns this applicant down.
post.description: Send `reason` to record why; it is stored on the application and shown to the worker.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/applications/{id}/select — books this applicant and takes one of the job's slots.
post.description:
The agreed pay falls back to the proposal made while shortlisting and then to the
pay on the posting, so the common case needs no body at all. The slot is taken
with a conditional database update, so two givers confirming the last worker at
once produce one booking and one 409 rather than an over-filled job.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/assignments/{id}/check-in — the worker confirms they are on site.
post.description:
The four-digit code is read out by the employer. It is single use, so a second
attempt with the same code is refused and the worker has to ask for a new one.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/assignments/{id}/complete — closes the booking once the work is done.
post.description:
Either the worker or the employer may close it, and `overtimeAmount` may be
recorded here so it is part of the payout. Closing the last live booking closes
the job, which is what allows both sides to leave a rating.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/auth/register — creates an unverified account and sends the OTP.
post.description:
The Flutter flow is register → /otp → role selection → profile setup, so this
endpoint returns `requiresOtpVerification: true` and a token pair that
the app stores while the code is entered.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/auth/verify-otp — confirms the phone and completes registration.
POST /api/v1/auth/resend-otp — issues a fresh code, superseding any outstanding one.
POST /api/v1/auth/login — signs in with an email address or a mobile number.
POST /api/v1/auth/refresh — rotates the refresh token and returns a new pair.
post.description: Presenting an already-rotated token revokes the whole token family as theft.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/auth/logout — revokes one session, or every session when no token is sent.
POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password — always the same response, registered or not.
POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password — verifies the code and revokes all sessions.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/jobs/{jobId}/check-in-code/{assignmentId} — read the code out.
get.description:
The employer opens their job, taps a booking and reads the four digits to the
worker on site. The code is per booking, single use, and never sent to the
worker: a worker asking for their own code would be able to check in unsupervised.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/devices — the caller's registered devices.

delete.summary: DELETE /api/v1/devices — stops push reaching every device.
delete.description: Called on sign-out, so the next person to sign in on that phone starts clean.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/devices/register — registers or refreshes one device.
post.description:
The app sends this on every launch, which is what makes it the place a device is
reactivated: a user who switched notifications back on in settings gets them
working simply by opening the app. Registering a token that is already known
updates it rather than creating a second row, and a token that belonged to another
account is moved across.

delete.summary: DELETE /api/v1/devices/{id} — stops push reaching one device.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/disputes — raises a dispute about a booking.
post.description:
Only the two participants can raise one, and the other party is worked out from the
booking, so a complaint cannot be aimed at somebody uninvolved. The other side is
notified immediately.
            
Send `amount` only when the dispute is about pay. Naming an amount holds the
booking's settled payment while the dispute is open; a dispute about the workplace
itself should leave `amount` at zero and hold nobody's money. One open dispute
per person per job.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/disputes — disputes the caller raised or was named in.
get.description:
Newest first, and both sides: a worker who has been complained about needs to see
the case and answer it. Pass `status=open` for a tab of what is still live.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/disputes/{id} — one dispute, for a participant.
get.description:
Includes the admin's resolution notes once it has been closed. Somebody who is not a
party to it is told the dispute does not exist rather than that it is off limits.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/giver/jobs — the caller's own postings, newest first.
GET /api/v1/giver/stats — the counters on the giver home screen.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/jobs — creates a job from the six-step wizard.
post.description:
Requires the `WorkGiver` role. The wizard posts once, so the default is a
published job; send `publishImmediately: false` to keep it as a draft and
call `POST /jobs/{id}/publish` later.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/jobs — searches published jobs.
get.description:
Supports `search`, `categories`, `statuses`, `area`,
`minPay`/`maxPay`, `startDate`/`endDate`, `jobType`,
`workplaceType`, `urgentOnly`, `recurringOnly`,
`verifiedGiverOnly` and a `latitude`/`longitude`/`radiusKm`
combination. Drafts are never returned.

put.summary: PUT /api/v1/jobs/{id} — edits a job. Only the fields you send change.
put.description: Only the poster can edit, and only while the job is still editable.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/jobs/{id} — one job, with the applicant count and your distance.
get.description:
A job whose address is hidden returns an empty `address` and null
coordinates until you are booked on it.

delete.description:
A job that has been published must be cancelled instead, so its applications
and payments keep a valid history.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/apply — a worker applies to an open job.
post.description:
Refused for a draft, a closed job, a full job, a passed deadline or an application
the worker already has, with the reason in `errorCode`. Applying twice is a
409, not a second row.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/applications — the applicants for a job the caller posted.
get.description:
Opening the list marks unseen applications as viewed. Filter with
`statuses`, `search` (worker name, area or phone), `minRating` and
`sortBy` (newest, oldest, ratingHigh, ratingLow, expectedPayHigh,
expectedPayLow, name).

post.summary: POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/select-workers — books several applicants in one call.
post.description:
The Flutter confirm-selection step sends every chosen applicant with the pay
agreed for each. The batch is all or nothing: if the job cannot fit all of them,
nothing is booked. Set `releaseUnselectedShortlists` to false to keep
shortlisted-but-not-selected applicants on the shortlist.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/publish — flips a draft live.
POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel — cancels the job and closes everything attached to it.
post.description:
Applicants and booked workers are notified, open applications are expired and
outstanding bookings are cancelled, so no party is left with a live-looking job.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/start — marks the job in progress.
post.description: Requires at least one booked worker, and only the poster may start it.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/complete — marks the job completed, which unlocks ratings.
POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/remind — nudges the workers who have not checked in.
post.description:
The employer's answer to a no-show. Only workers on the job who have not checked in
yet are messaged, and only once the job is actually running, so a reminder can never
reach a booking that is not due. The answer says how many were reminded, which is
what the app shows in the toast.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/jobs/{jobId}/payments/{workerId} — releases pay for one booking.
post.description:
Sends `basePay`, optional `overtime` and the `method`; the 5%
platform fee and the totals are worked out server side so the client cannot
disagree with them. Supply `idempotencyKey` to make a retry explicit —
without one, a stable key is derived from the booking, so a repeated request
returns the original receipt instead of paying twice.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/media/profile-images/{fileName} — an avatar.
GET /api/v1/media/documents/{fileName} — an identity or skill document.
GET /api/v1/conversations — the caller's threads, most recently active first.
get.description:
Each row carries the other person's name, the job the thread is about, the unread
count and the last message. A thread with no messages yet still appears, sorted
last, so a conversation opened from a job card is visible immediately. Pass
`includeArchived=true` to see threads that have been cleared from the list.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/conversations — opens, or re-opens, the thread with one person.
post.description:
Send the other person's `participantId` and, when the question is about a
particular job, its `jobId`. Both people must have been involved in that job.
Asking for the same pair about the same job twice returns the thread that already
exists rather than a second copy, so the job card's Message button and the chat
list cannot end up with two threads between the same two people.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/conversations/{id} — the header of one thread.
get.description: The other person's name, the job context and the unread count, for the chat screen's title bar.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/conversations/{id}/messages — one page of a thread, oldest first.
get.description:
`newestFirst=true` (the default the app uses) returns the most recent page in
            reading order, which is what a chat screen wants: page 1 is the bottom of the
            conversation. Pass `newestFirst=false` to walk backwards through history.
            Reading does not clear the badge — POST `/read` does, so the badge drops when
            the screen opens rather than when a page of messages happens to arrive.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/messages — posts one message.
post.description:
The other participant's unread count goes up and they get a notification, so the
message reaches them whether or not they are looking at the app. The sender's own
badge stays at zero and the thread returns to the top of their list.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/read — clears this thread's unread badge.
post.description:
Answers with how many messages were cleared, which is what the app subtracts from
its local badge without a second round trip. Calling it on an already-read thread
is accepted and returns 0, so a retried screen open is harmless.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/archive — clears a thread from the list.
post.description:
Hides the thread for the caller only and drops its unread count, so the badge stops
counting a conversation that is no longer on screen. Nothing is deleted: the other
person keeps their copy, and sending a new message in that thread brings it back.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/notifications — the caller's notifications, newest first.
get.description:
Optional filters: `unreadOnly` and `types` (repeatable, e.g.
`?types=payment&types=jobAccepted`). The app's type filter chips map
straight onto the second one.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count — both badge counts in one call.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/notifications/{id}/read — marks one row read.
post.description:
The app calls this as soon as a row is tapped, before it navigates, so the badge
drops even if the target screen cannot be opened. Answering with the remaining
unread count saves the app a second round trip just to redraw its badge. Marking
an already-read row is accepted, so a retried tap is harmless.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/notifications/read-all — marks every unread row read.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/payments — the caller's own payments, newest first.
get.description:
Scoped by role: a giver sees what they paid out, a worker what they received, an
administrator everything. Optional filters: `statuses`, `jobId`,
`workerId`, `from`, `to`.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/confirm — settles a payment the gateway left in flight.
post.description:
A real gateway will call this from a signed webhook. Until one is wired up the
giver who made the payment may confirm it by hand. Confirming a payment that is
already settled is a no-op, so a duplicated callback is harmless.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/refund — reverses a settled payment. Administrator only.
post.description:
Deliberately not available to the giver or the worker: reversing a charge moves
money back out of the platform, so only an administrator can do it and the
reason is recorded on the payment.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/profile/me — everything the profile screen shows.
GET /api/v1/profile/{userId} — another user's public profile.
get.description:
No phone number, email or coordinates. The app shows this from a chat thread and
from an application, and contact details are exchanged in the conversation itself.

put.summary: PUT /api/v1/profile/worker — saves the worker edit-profile form.
put.description:
Partial: send only what changed, and `skills` replaces the whole list. Omit
`skills` to leave it alone; send `[]` to clear it.

put.summary: PUT /api/v1/profile/giver — saves the employer edit-profile form.
PUT /api/v1/profile/availability — replaces the weekly availability grid.
put.description:
The whole week in one call, because the app edits it as one screen. An empty
`slots` array clears the week.

Call with `isOnline: true` when the app comes to the foreground and false when
it is backgrounded. This is the flag behind the green dot in the chat list.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/profile/image — uploads a profile photo and attaches it.
post.description:
Multipart with a single `file` part. JPEG, PNG, WebP or PDF up to the
configured limit. The previous photo is left on disk and simply stops being linked,
so a failed re-upload cannot leave the profile with no image.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/profile/documents — uploads an identity or skill document.
post.description:
Multipart: a `file` part and a `type` field of identity, phone, email,
skills or address. The document is stored and listed as pending; send its
`url` to `POST /verifications` to have it reviewed. Documents are private
to the worker who uploaded them and to an admin.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/ratings — rates the other participant in a completed job.
post.description:
Send the `jobId` and who is being rated. An employer rates the worker and a
worker rates the employer; one rating per person per job, and only after the job
is completed. The rating updates that person's average straight away.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/ratings — feedback received, newest first.
get.description:
With no filter this is the caller's own feedback. Pass `toUserId` to read
someone else's, and `jobId` to see only what was said about one job.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/worker/saved-jobs — the bookmarked jobs, newest bookmark first.
get.description:
Only active jobs by default. Pass `includeClosed=true` to see jobs that have
since been filled, completed or cancelled; the bookmark itself is never removed
automatically.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/worker/saved-jobs/{jobId} — bookmarks a job.
post.description: Saving a job that is already saved returns the existing bookmark.

delete.description: Reports whether a bookmark was actually there, so the app can refresh either way.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/support-reports — files a report for the team to look at.
post.description:
Describe the problem in a sentence or two. `relatedJobId` is optional; include
it when the report is about one particular booking so the admin can open it.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/verifications — the badge plus the history behind it.
get.description:
Returns the overall badge, the state of each individual check, and every attempt
newest first. Pass `type` to list only one kind of check — that is what a
checklist row's "try again" link uses.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/verifications — asks for one kind of check to be reviewed.
post.description:
Send the `documentUrl` returned by `POST /profile/documents` to attach the
uploaded file. One live request per type: asking again while one is pending is a
409, because two open requests for the same check leave an admin with no way to tell
which document is current.
            
Phone and email checks are refused up front if the account has no number or address
to check — a request an admin could only ever reject is not worth sending.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/verifications/summary — the badge on its own.
get.description:
Cheap enough to call from the app shell on any screen. `overall` is
`verified` only when identity, phone, email and skills are all approved; a
rejection anywhere outranks that.

post.summary: POST /api/v1/verifications/{id}/withdraw — takes a pending request back.
post.description:
Not a delete: the attempt stays in the history, recorded as withdrawn, so it is
clear the applicant chose to stop rather than being refused. Only a pending request
can be withdrawn.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/worker/earnings — one wallet line per booking.
get.description:
A booking appears as soon as it is made, with its money still pending, and is
never listed twice: the line is keyed by the booking, not by the payment.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/worker/earnings/summary — earned and pending money per month.
GET /api/v1/worker/wallet — earned, pending and disputed totals.
GET /api/v1/worker/jobs — jobs a worker can still apply to.
get.description:
Supports the same filters as `GET /jobs`, plus a radius search around
`latitude`/`longitude` that returns a `distanceKm` per job.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/worker/stats — application, booking and earnings counters.
GET /api/v1/worker/applications — the caller's own applications.
get.description:
Newest first. Filter with `statuses` (for example `shortlisted`) and with
`jobStatus` to see only applications for jobs that are still running.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/worker/work-history — the signed-in worker's bookings.
get.description:
A booking is listed as soon as it is made; `paymentStatus` is what
distinguishes work agreed from work paid. Optional filters: `from`, `to`,
`paymentStatus`, `jobId`.

get.summary: GET /api/v1/giver/work-history — the signed-in employer's bookings.
get.description: The counterpart on each line is the worker, and earnings are what they were paid.

tags.name: AdminAuth
tags.description:
The admin console's sign-in. Separate from Jobmate.Api.Controllers.AuthController because
the admin surface is email-only and a non-admin account must never be able to
authenticate here even with a correct password.

tags.name: Admin
tags.description:
The admin back office: the dashboard, the verification review queue, and the user and
job tables.
            
The `Admin` role is required on the whole controller, so every endpoint here is
unreachable to a worker or a work giver, and each read goes through a MediatR query
rather than a direct database call.
            
These are the only endpoints that return phone numbers, email addresses and exact
areas for other people. That is deliberate and confined to this controller: an admin
has to be able to identify and contact the person in front of them, and the privacy
rules for the marketplace itself are enforced by the user-facing projections rather
than by hiding fields from this one screen.

tags.name: Application
tags.description:
Actions on a single application: the worker's withdraw and the giver's shortlist or
reject. Applying lives on the job route (POST /jobs/{id}/apply) and the two lists
live there too, so this controller only holds the actions keyed by application id.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description:
Authentication: registration with phone OTP, sign-in, token rotation and
password recovery. These are the only endpoints that do not require a bearer
token.

tags.name: Dispute
tags.description: Raising and tracking a dispute about a booking.

tags.name: SupportReport
tags.description:
Reporting a problem. Separate from Jobmate.Api.Controllers.DisputeController because a report
needs no booking: a fake job listing somebody only ever saw has no other party to
argue with, and refusing to let anybody report those would lose exactly the abuse
cases that matter most.

tags.name: AdminTrust
tags.description:
The admin side of disputes and support reports. Lives on the admin route so the whole
controller inherits the Admin role requirement.

tags.name: Job
tags.description:
Job postings: the create/edit lifecycle for a work giver, the public search feed
and the worker's discovery list. Every action is a MediatR request; this class only
binds, authorises and wraps the result in the standard response envelope.

tags.name: GiverJobs
tags.description:
The work giver's own job list and home-screen counters. Kept off
`/jobs` because the route is always scoped to the caller and never accepts a
giver id, which is what stops one employer reading another's postings.

tags.name: WorkerJobs
tags.description:
The worker's discovery feed and home-screen counters. `GET /worker/jobs` only
ever returns open jobs with a free worker slot.

tags.name: Messaging
tags.description:
Chat between the two people on a job.
            
Delivery is by polling: the app opens a thread and re-reads it on an interval, which
keeps chat on the same REST surface as everything else and leaves the unread counter on
the database as the single source of truth. Nothing here is written specifically for
polling — a message is persisted and summarised in one operation — so a push-based
transport can be added later without the handlers changing.
            
Every route is scoped to the signed-in caller by the handlers, and no route accepts
anybody else's id, so there is no way to read a conversation you are not in.

tags.name: Notification
tags.description:
The caller's notification inbox: the list, the unread badge, and marking rows read.
            
Every route here is scoped to the signed-in caller by the handlers, so there is no way
to address another user's notifications.

tags.name: Device
tags.description:
Push device registration — the tokens a notification is delivered to.
            
Registration is keyed on the provider token, so a phone that changes hands is
re-pointed at the new account instead of silently keeping the old one's notifications.

tags.name: Payment
tags.description:
Money: releasing pay for a booking, listing the caller's payments, and the
administrator's refund.
            
Creating a payment hangs off the job route, because the app releases pay from a
job and names the worker: POST /jobs/{jobId}/payments/{workerId}. The remaining
actions are keyed by payment id and live here.

tags.name: WorkerEarnings
tags.description:
The worker wallet: earnings, month-grouped totals and the summary the earnings
screen header shows.

tags.name: JobPayment
tags.description:
The giver side of releasing pay. Separate from Jobmate.Api.Controllers.PaymentController
because the route is nested under a job: the app releases pay from a job and names
the worker it is paying.

tags.name: Profile
tags.description:
The caller's own profile, and the reduced public view of anyone else's.
            
Two shapes rather than one on purpose: the owner screen needs phone, email and
documents, and none of that may reach a stranger. The public endpoint returns a
different type so those fields cannot be added back by accident.

tags.name: Media
tags.description:
Serves uploaded files back.
            
Split into two routes because the two families have different audiences: a profile
photo is shown to anyone signed in, while an identity document is readable only by the
worker who uploaded it and by an admin. One route for both would mean either
publishing everyone's passports or hiding every avatar.

tags.name: Assignment
tags.description:
A booking's own actions: proving attendance and closing the work off.
            
These hang off the assignment rather than the job because they act on one booking:
a job with three workers has three check-ins and three completions.

tags.name: CheckInCode
tags.description: The employer-facing half of check-in: the code the worker has to type in.

tags.name: Rating
tags.description:
Feedback between the two sides of a finished job, and the feedback a person has
received.

tags.name: WorkHistory
tags.description:
Work history for either side. The endpoint is the same shape for both roles; the
counterpart on each line is whoever the other party is.

tags.name: SavedJobs
tags.description:
A worker's bookmarked jobs.
            
The bookmark list is per user and per job, and both adding and removing are idempotent:
a double tap on the save icon is not an error, and neither is unsaving something that
is not saved.

tags.name: Verification
tags.description:
The trust badge, and the requests behind it.
            
Reads and withdrawals are the user's own; the decision itself is an admin action on
`/admin/verifications`. Splitting them is what stops a user approving themselves.
